newsitem.title: USA: Florida Lottery raises $7 billion for schools.
newsitem.headline: Florida Lottery raises $7 billion for schools.

text.p: The Florida Lottery has contributed a record $7 billion to state schools since the games were introduced nine years ago, Lottery Secretary Marcia Mann said Thursday.
"No other Lottery in the nation has ever earned so much so quickly. In fiscal year 1995-96 alone, the Florida Lottery generated $820 million for education in Florida," Mann said.
The lottery has begun an advetising campaign to combat "the fallacies that exist" about the way lottery proceeds are used.

Polls have shown that many residents feel schools were shortchanged by the lottery because the constitutional amendment that established it said the proceeds would be used for "enhancements" of education.
But as the lottery money came in, the legislature cut education allocations from the general fund budget, using the lottery money as a replacement rather than an enhancement.
Mann said the lottery "goes above and beyond what is required of it and has, since the first ticket was sold."
Individual school districts decide how to use the lottery money earmarked for education, she said.
On a statewide level, Florida used lottery proceeds to establish the Pre-Kindergarten Early Prevention program aimed at preparing at-risk youngsters for the classroom.
"The Pre-K program has helped more than 200,000 children throughout Florida's 67 school districts to achieve school readiness," Mann said.
